The refusal is raised only on the _mysql_parse_sql path, which assert_select_only (433) enters only when type(parser_dialect) is MySQL or the base sqlglot.Dialect. CHANGELOG.md:78 and docs/external/release-notes.md:13 carry the same four points: boundary rejection for MySQL and unspecified/default dialects, doubled quotes instead of backslash-escaped quotes, spaces between adjacent minus signs, and LF/CRLF instead of bare CR in line comments for the default dialect. Code matches: assert_select_only applies _mysql_parse_sql only for MySQL or the base Dialect (readonly.py:432-433). That function rejects backslash-escaped quotes (372-374), rejects '--' followed by a non-whitespace character (395-398), and rejects a bare CR in line comments only when mysql_line_comments is false, i.e. the default dialect (404-409). It also rejects /*! and /*M! executable comments (386-387).
